title: Administrative units: which users can a delegated administrator manage?
summary: The page overstates the protection provided by restricted management units: some changes remain available without a unit-scoped role, including licence assignment and usage-location updates. The documented control paths and commands check out, with minor corrections needed to the membership API note and the description of bulk membership operations.

claims.claim: An Entra administrative unit can contain only users, groups or devices.
claims.quote: An administrative unit can contain only users, groups, or devices.

claims.where: summary; What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Unit-scoped Entra roles limit management permissions to the unit's members rather than granting tenant-wide management.
claims.quote: When a Microsoft Entra role is assigned at the scope of an administrative unit, role permissions apply only when managing members of the administrative unit itself, and don't apply to tenant-wide settings or configurations.

claims.claim: Administrative units can be managed through the Entra admin center, PowerShell and Microsoft Graph.
claims.quote: You can manage administrative units by using the Microsoft Entra admin center, PowerShell cmdlets and scripts, or Microsoft Graph API.

claims.claim: A user can belong to multiple administrative units.
claims.quote: Users can be members of multiple administrative units.

claims.where: What it is: The unit; Risks and limits: No nesting
claims.claim: Administrative units cannot be nested.
claims.quote: Administrative units can't be nested.

claims.claim: Users, groups and devices can be added manually to administrative units.
claims.quote: This article describes how to add users, groups, or devices to administrative units manually.

claims.claim: Users, groups and devices can be added to administrative units in bulk.
claims.quote: Entries: Object Ids or UPN of members to add to the Admin Unit. Rename the file if desired, then select and upload the edited file.
claims.fix: The broader bulk-operations source is titled 'Bulk operations in Microsoft Entra ID (Preview)' and is not cited. Avoid expanding the sources or implying final availability by replacing the Members bullet's first sentence with: 'Users, groups and devices can be added manually. Users can also be added in bulk, and users and devices by dynamic membership rules.' The existing cited admin-units-members-add page supports that narrower statement.

claims.claim: Dynamic membership rules can manage users and devices in administrative units.
claims.quote: For information about how to add users or devices to administrative units dynamically using rules, see Manage users or devices for an administrative unit with rules for dynamic membership groups.

claims.where: What it is: Members; controls[2].note; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Adding a group scopes management of the group itself, not its members.
claims.quote: Adding a group to an administrative unit brings the group itself into the management scope of the administrative unit, but not the members of the group.

claims.where: What it is: Scoped role assignments
claims.claim: A User Administrator assigned at unit scope manages the members, not the administrative unit itself.
claims.quote: The scope /administrativeUnits/<ID> means the principal can manage the members of the administrative unit (based on the role that the principal is assigned), not the administrative unit itself.

claims.where: What it is: Scoped role assignments
claims.claim: Unit-scoped administrators can use the Microsoft 365 admin center for basic management of their units' users.
claims.quote: Administrative unit-scoped admins can use the Microsoft 365 admin center for basic management of users in their administrative units.

claims.where: What it is: Scoped role assignments
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center filters out users outside the scoped administrator's units.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, users outside a scoped admin's administrative units are filtered out.

claims.where: What it is: Restricted management units
claims.claim: Restricted management prevents anyone, including Global Administrators, from changing member objects unless assigned a unit-scoped role.
claims.quote: operations that directly modify the Microsoft Entra properties of objects in restricted management administrative units are blocked, whereas operations on related objects in Microsoft 365 services aren't affected.
claims.fix: Qualify the Restricted management units bullet rather than promising protection from all changes. Replace it with: 'A variant that restricts direct modification of members' Microsoft Entra properties to explicitly assigned unit-scoped administrators. Related Microsoft 365 operations are not affected; assigning licences and updating users' usage location also remain allowed. Global Administrators can still manage the unit itself and assign themselves a unit-scoped role.' The cited page's operations table explicitly allows those exceptions.

claims.where: What it is: Restricted management units
claims.claim: Global Administrators can manage restricted management units themselves and assign themselves scoped roles.
claims.quote: Assign roles to themselves with restricted management administrative units scope

claims.where: What it is: In Microsoft Purview; Why it matters
claims.claim: Restricted administrators create and manage supported policies for users in their assigned units.
claims.quote: Restricted administrators can create or manage policies only for users assigned to their administrative units.

claims.where: What it is: In Microsoft Purview; Why it matters
claims.claim: Supported alert and activity visibility is scoped to the restricted administrator's assigned units.
claims.quote: Going forward, restricted administrators can see this related data for their assigned administrative units only.

claims.where: What it is: In Microsoft Purview; Risks and limits; controls[6].note
claims.claim: Purview SharePoint-site membership supports auto-labelling and DLP policies that apply to SharePoint sites only.
claims.quote: This support is only available for Microsoft Information Protection auto-labeling policies and Microsoft Data Loss Prevention policies that support application to SharePoint sites.

claims.claim: Copilot, Copilot Chat and Cowork DLP unit scoping matches the user submitting the prompt, not the content owner.
claims.quote: DLP policy scoping for Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork is based on the user who submits the prompt, not the owner of a file or email that the experience accesses.

claims.claim: Units scope management permissions but do not prevent default-permission browsing outside the unit.
claims.quote: They don't prevent members or administrators from using their default user permissions to browse other users, groups, or resources outside the administrative unit.

claims.claim: After unit assignment, restricted administrators cannot see or edit existing policies, which remain available to unrestricted administrators.
claims.quote: After you assign administrative units to members of the role groups, these restricted administrators can't see and edit existing policies. However, there's no operational change to these policies and they remain visible and can be edited by unrestricted administrators.

claims.claim: Restricted administrators lose visibility of historical activity explorer and alert data, which remains visible to unrestricted administrators.
claims.quote: Restricted administrators also can't see historical data by using features that support administrative units, such as activity explorer and alerts. They remain visible to unrestricted administrators.

claims.claim: Creating administrative units is available with Entra ID Free.
claims.quote: Creating administrative units is available with a Microsoft Entra ID Free license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Microsoft Purview; Open questions
claims.claim: The Purview administrative-units page does not specify which users the Entra licence is counted for.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview administrative units P1 P2 license which administrators role group scoped members'; read purview-admin-units prerequisites and linked admin-units-manage prerequisites. The Purview page lists P1/P2 but gives no per-user counting rule.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group membership does not flow
claims.claim: A scoped administrator can change the name and membership of a group in the administrative unit.
claims.quote: an administrator scoped to the administrative unit can manage properties of the group, such as group name or membership

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group membership does not flow
claims.claim: Scoping a group does not permit editing its members' properties or passwords unless the users are directly added to the unit.
claims.quote: they cannot manage properties of the users or devices within that group (unless those users and devices are separately added as members of the administrative unit).

claims.where: Risks and limits: Group membership does not flow
claims.claim: Dynamic distribution group membership does not automatically confer administrative unit membership.
claims.quote: Members of Dynamic Distribution Groups don't automatically become members of an administrative unit.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Dynamic units hold no groups
claims.claim: An administrative unit using dynamic membership rules cannot contain groups.
claims.quote: You can't add groups to an administrative unit that uses dynamic membership rules.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Dynamic units hold no groups
claims.claim: Microsoft advises creating separate user and group units where needed.
claims.quote: If needed, create two administrative units, one for users and one for groups.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Insider Risk Management alerts for group-added users are hidden
claims.claim: Only unrestricted administrators can access IRM alerts for users included through security or distribution groups in units.
claims.quote: Restricted administrators can't access alerts for the users assigned to them through security groups or distribution groups added in administrative units. Such user alerts are visible only to unrestricted administrators.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Insider Risk Management alerts for group-added users are hidden
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends adding users directly to units to make their alerts visible to restricted administrators.
claims.quote: Microsoft recommends adding users directly to administrative units to ensure their alerts are also visible to restricted administrators with administrative units assigned.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits; What to check
claims.claim: Restricted management must be configured at creation and cannot subsequently be changed.
claims.quote: The restricted management setting must be applied during administrative unit creation and can't be changed once the administrative unit is created.

claims.claim: A tenant can have at most 100 restricted management administrative units.
claims.quote: A maximum of 100 restricted management administrative units in a tenant.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Restricted management is fixed at creation
claims.claim: Users and groups in restricted management units cannot be managed with the named Entra ID Governance features.
claims.quote: Groups and users in a restricted management administrative unit can't be managed with Microsoft Entra ID Governance features such as Privileged Identity Management, Entitlement management, Lifecycle workflows and Access reviews.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Defender XDR scopes only DLP

claims.quote: Although DLP and Insider Risk Management both surface alerts in Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Defender XDR only supports administrative units for DLP.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Defender XDR scopes only DLP
claims.claim: Defender XDR supports up to 100 administrative units.
claims.quote: Microsoft Defender XDR supports up to 100 administrative units.

claims.where: Risks and limits: SharePoint site queries are slow and coarse
claims.claim: A SharePoint-site query can take up to five days to populate.
claims.quote: It can take up to five days for a SharePoint site query to fully populate.

claims.where: Risks and limits: SharePoint site queries are slow and coarse
claims.claim: Administrators selecting administrative units cannot include or exclude individual SharePoint sites.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Intune is outside it
claims.claim: Administrative units do not support managing devices in Intune.
claims.quote: Managing devices in Intune is not supported at this time.

claims.claim: Creating a unit in the Entra admin center requires at least Privileged Role Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a Privileged Role Administrator.

claims.quote:
To add existing users, groups, or devices:
Privileged Role Administrator

claims.claim: Assigning unit-scoped roles in the Entra admin center requires at least Privileged Role Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a Privileged Role Administrator.

claims.claim: Assigning units to Purview role-group members requires Role management.
claims.quote: To assign a role group member to an administrative unit, administrators must be assigned the Role management role.

claims.claim: Configuring SharePoint-site associations requires the admin unit extension manager role.
claims.quote: To complete the following steps to configure SharePoint sites within administrative units for use in Microsoft Purview, you must have the admin unit extension manager role assigned.

claims.claim: Site membership queries support site URL, site name and RefinableString00 through RefinableString99.
claims.quote: Queries to associate SharePoint sites with administrative units support site properties for Site URL, site name, and RefinableString00-RefinableString99.

claims.claim: The unit's role picker offers roles with permissions relevant to objects supported in administrative units.

claims.claim: Unit scoping does not replace solution permissions; DLP unit administrators still need the same DLP roles or role groups.
claims.quote: Administrative unit admins need to be assigned to one of the same roles or role groups as administrators of unrestricted DLP policies in order to create and manage DLP policies for their administrative unit.

claims.claim: Restricted administrators must select one or more units when configuring supported policies.

claims.claim: Unrestricted administrators can retain whole-directory policy scope or select administrative units.
claims.quote: They can keep the default of the entire directory or select one or more administrative units.

claims.claim: The creation path is Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Roles & admins > Admin units > Add.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > Roles & admins > Admin units.
Select Add.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/directory/administrativeUnits creates an administrative unit.
claims.quote:
Use the Create administrativeUnit API to create a new administrative unit.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/directory/administrativeUnits

claims.claim: The restricted-management toggle is under Entra ID > Roles & admins > Admin units > Add > Restricted management administrative unit.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > Roles & admins > Admin units.
Select Add.
If you don't want tenant-level administrators to be able to access this administrative unit, set the Restricted management administrative unit toggle to Yes.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/directory/administrativeUnits with isMemberManagementRestricted creates a restricted management unit.
claims.quote:
Use the Create administrativeUnit API to create a new restricted management administrative unit. Set the isMemberManagementRestricted property to true.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/directory/administrativeUnits

claims.claim: The member-addition path is Entra ID > Roles & admins > Admin units > administrative unit > Users > Add member, with Groups > Add and Devices > Add device alternatives.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > Roles & admins > Admin units.
Select the administrative unit you want to add users, groups, or devices to.
Select one of the following:
Users
Groups
Devices
Select Add member, Add, or Add device.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/directory/administrativeUnits/{id}/members/$ref adds an existing user, group or device.
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged and append to controls[2].note: 'The request body sets @odata.id to the URL of the user, group or device to add.' Mirror that note in the rendered table.

claims.claim: Unit-scoped role assignment uses Entra ID > Roles & admins > Admin units > administrative unit > Roles and administrators > role > Add assignments.
claims.quote:
Select Roles and administrators from the left navigation menu to see the list of all roles available to be assigned over an administrative unit.
Select the desired role.
Select Add assignments and then select the users or groups you want to assign this role to.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments sets unit scope through directoryScopeId = /administrativeUnits/<ID>.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments
...
"directoryScopeId": "/administrativeUnits/<Object ID of administrative unit>"

claims.claim: The Purview role-group route through Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > member > Assign admin units reaches the unit assignment control.
claims.quote: To update the administrative units for users or groups, select any of the currently assigned user or groups and select Assign admin units.

claims.claim: For the Copilot location, Purview uses Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Admin units.
claims.quote:
go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy.
Select the Custom template, then Custom policy, and enter a name and description.
On the Admin units page, select the administrative units for the policy.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <String> -PolicyRBACScopes <administrative-unit-ObjectID> sets DLP policy administrative units in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote:
This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
...
The PolicyRBACScopes parameter specifies the administrative units to assign to the policy. A valid value is the Microsoft Entra ObjectID (GUID value) of the administrative unit.

claims.claim: SharePoint site association uses Purview Settings > Roles and scopes > Administrative units > administrative unit > Edit.
claims.quote:
Select Settings and select Roles and scopes.
Select Administrative units.
Select an existing administrative unit from the list.
Select Edit.
Create a query to associate SharePoint sites with the administrative unit.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or Graph operation is documented for assigning administrative units to Purview role-group members.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview administrative units assign role group members PowerShell Add-RoleGroupMember AdministrativeUnits parameter'; '"Add-RoleGroupMember" "Administrative"'. Read purview-admin-units, purview-permissions and Add-RoleGroupMember. No unit-setting operation.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or Graph operation is documented for configuring Purview SharePoint-site membership queries.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview administrative units SharePoint site query PowerShell Graph API administrative unit extension'; '"Purview" "administrative units" "SharePoint" "Set-AdministrativeUnit"'. Read purview-admin-units and Graph administrativeUnit search excerpts. No site-query setter.

claims.claim: Administrative-unit support for the Copilot, Copilot Chat and Cowork DLP location is in preview.
claims.quote: Administrative unit support for this location, including Cowork, is in preview and is rolling out. The option might not yet be available in your tenant.
